c.tagline: Kerala's laid-back capital — the golden Padmanabhaswamy Temple, palm-fringed Kovalam sands, and the gateway to the backwaters.

taxi.fareNote: Autos are metered but drivers often prefer a negotiated fare — agree it first, or book via Uber/Ola for a fixed price. Prepaid taxi counters operate at the airport and Central station.

emergency.note: 112 is India's single all-services emergency number; 108 reaches ambulance services and 100 the police.

avoid.reason: Avoid isolated stretches of Shanghumugham beach after dark and watch belongings in the East Fort market crowds; agree auto-rickshaw fares upfront.

hood_desc: The historic heart around the golden-gopuram Sri Padmanabhaswamy Temple, the Kuthira Malika palace and the buzzing Chalai bazaar; the most atmospheric, traditional part of the city and close to the Central railway station.

The central civic and cultural belt along MG Road, taking in the Napier Museum, Sri Chitra Art Gallery, the zoo, the Secretariat and Palayam's mosque-church-temple cluster; the walkable middle of the city.

Kerala's most famous beach resort, 16 km south — a crescent of sand below a candy-striped lighthouse, lined with seafood shacks, Ayurveda spas and hotels from backpacker to five-star. Relaxed and holiday-minded.
The green, modern IT city on the northern edge around Technopark and Kazhakkoottam, with newer hotels, malls and easy airport access; convenient and quiet rather than sightseeing-central.

A tranquil island where the backwaters meet the sea about 30 km south, all coconut palms, lagoon cruises and resort jetties — the gentle gateway to Kerala's backwaters for those wanting calm over city bustle.
lodging: Isola Di Cocco Ayurvedic Beach Resort

water.note: Drink bottled or filtered water and skip ice of unknown origin.

transit.hours: KSRTC and private city buses run roughly 5:30 AM to 10:00 PM; ride apps and autos cover the late-night gap.
transit.note: Thiruvananthapuram has no metro. KSRTC and private buses are the backbone of city transport, with metered and app-booked auto-rickshaws widely available. Tourist boats run the backwaters and lagoons from Kovalam, Poovar and Veli, and beaches line the coast south of the city.
transit.pay: Bus fares are paid in cash to the conductor on board. Autos are cash or app; agree an auto fare before you board. There is no rechargeable city transit card.

bus: KSRTC intercity buses from Thampanoor across Kerala and to Kanyakumari

transit.m: City bus to Thampanoor / East Fort (~30 min)
Prepaid taxi to the city centre (15-20 min)

tip.r: Not customary; rounding up or leaving 5-10% at nicer restaurants and resorts is appreciated but not expected.
